dedupe_keys.name: global media and internet concentration project gmicp telecom internet and media market data for about 40 countries

description: The Global Media and Internet Concentration Project, a worldwide research network led by Dwayne Winseck of Carleton University, tracks about two dozen communication, internet and media markets in nearly 40 countries and asks whether they are becoming more or less concentrated. For each country it publishes open reports and workbooks with the major companies, their revenues and market shares, and concentration measures (concentration ratios and the Herfindahl-Hirschman index) for mobile wireless and wireline telecoms, broadband internet access, cable, satellite and IPTV, broadcasting, streaming, search, social media, app stores and more. Canada's workbooks run from 1984 to 2024 and the United States from 1984 to 2023; teams have covered Argentina, Australia, Austria, Brazil, Chile, China, the Czech Republic, France, India, Italy, Mexico, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, South Africa, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland and others, mostly for 2019 to 2023, and a dashboard compares them. Coverage: about 40 countries. Format and access: Excel workbooks and PDF reports on Borealis and the project website, free of charge and open access. Caveats: revenues and shares are compiled from company reports and estimates; sector definitions vary slightly by country. Simulation uses: operator market shares for modelling the effect of an operator's outage on customers, and market structure for resilience and regulation studies. Related records: ITU ICT statistics give national subscriptions; regulator open data give operator-level coverage.
